name: Clavulanic Acid
mechanism: Class A β-lactamase suicide inhibitor (irreversible acylation of active-site serine); TEM-1 is the canonical target.

tem1_nitrocefin.screen_rationale: Project positive-control concentration; ~60× above literature Ki (0.85 µM) — expect strong inhibition.
tem1_nitrocefin.metric: relative nitrocefin hydrolysis vs no-inhibitor control (initial slope or 10 min endpoint)

entries.title: A glycine at position 105 leads to clavulanic acid and avibactam resistance in class A β-lactamases
entries.note: Primary evidence: TEM-1 WT Ki = 0.85 µM for clavulanic acid in nitrocefin inhibition assay (Table 4). TEM-1 Y105G Ki = 5.15 µM. Methods: 0.25–0.25 nM TEM-1, clavulanic acid 0.25–5 µM, 200 µM nitrocefin, 10 µM BSA, 100 mM NaPi pH 6.4, 25 °C, A486 for 10 min.

entries.title: Characterization of Interactions between CTX-M-15 and Clavulanic Acid, Desfuroylceftiofur, Ceftiofur, Ampicillin, and Nitrocefin
entries.assay: ceftiofur hydrolysis (nitrocefin used for general kinetics)
entries.note: Supporting class-A precedent: clavulanic acid Ki = 0.022 µM vs CTX-M-15; clavulanic acid 0–50 µM, 10 nM enzyme, PBS pH 7.4, 37 °C.
